subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class per-profile managed-browser proxy config plus per-agent/subagent default browser-profile binding, and what security model should govern proxy credentials, SSRF enforcement, profile selection, inheritance, and concurrency limits?
rationale: Source inspection confirms the requested behavior remains missing, but implementing it defines new public config/API shape and browser egress/session security boundaries that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Approve a gated browser-profile design
options.body: Add the feature behind an explicit contract with SecretRef-safe proxy auth, SSRF trust gates, profile authorization and inheritance rules, launch/resource controls, observability, and focused docs/tests.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical tracks
options.body: Let #60035 own broader proxy policy and #85672 own browser ownership/inheritance semantics, then keep or close this umbrella only after owners confirm the split.

options.title: Document current workaround only
options.body: Keep using explicit tool profiles, browser.extraArgs, remote CDP or external browser-lock/FSB-style orchestration until the security and product model is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated browser-profile design
recommendation.body: Add the feature behind an explicit contract with SecretRef-safe proxy auth, SSRF trust gates, profile authorization and inheritance rules, launch/resource controls, observability, and focused docs/tests.
